abhts_8.1 yat tu katipayakatipayabhedānugataṃ rūpaṃ tat tattvaṃ yathā pṛthivī nāma dyutikāṭhinyasthaulyādirūpā kālāgniprabhṛtivīrabhadrāntabhuvaneśādhiṣṭhitasamastabrahmāṇḍānugatā // abhts_8.2 tatra eṣāṃ tattvānāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvo darśyate sa ca dvividhaḥ // abhts_8.3 pāramārthikaḥ sṛṣṭeś ca // abhts_8.4 tatra pāramārthika etāvān kāryakāraṇabhāvo yad uta kartṛsvabhāvasya svatantrasya bhagavata evaṃvidhena śivādidharāntena vapuṣā svarūpabhinnena svarūpaviśrāntena ca prathanam // abhts_8.5 kalpitas tu kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ parameśecchayā niyatiprāṇayā nirmitaḥ sa ca yāvati yadā niyatapaurvāparyāvabhāsanaṃ saty api adhike svarūpānugatam etāvaty eva tena yogīcchāto 'pi aṅkuro bījād api svapnādau ghaṭāder apīti // abhts_8.6 tatrāpi ca parameśvarasya kartṛtvānapāya iti akalpito 'pi asau pāramārthikaḥ sthita eva // abhts_8.7 pāramārthike hi bhittisthānīye sthite rūpe sarvam idam ullikhyamānaṃ ghaṭate na anyathā ata eva sāmagryā eva kāruṇatvaṃ yuktam // abhts_8.8 sā hi samastabhāvasaṃdarbhamayī svatantrasaṃvedanamahimnā tathā niyatanijanijadeśakālabhāvarāśisvabhāvā pratyekaṃ vastusvarūpaniṣpattisamaye tathābhūtā tathābhūtāyā hi anyathābhāvo yathā yathā adhikībhavati tathā tathā kāryasyāpi vijātīyatvaṃ tāratamyena puṣyati // abhts_8.9 ity evaṃ saṃvedanasvātantryasvabhāvaḥ parameśvara eva viśvabhāvaśarīro ghaṭāder nirmātā kumbhakārasaṃvidas tato 'nadhikatvāt l1_text:
## tsa08-p01
When this glory-natured world-host stated — wombing endless varied enjoyer-enjoyed — therein, what is united, great-light-natured, that is great-universal-like, supreme-Śiva-natured. (8.1) But what form is united with some-some differences, that is principle — as earth named, shining-hard-gross-formed, from time-fire to Vīrabhadra-end world-lord-abided whole-universe-egg-united. (8.2) Therein, of these principles, effect-cause-relation is shown; and it is twofold. (8.3) Ultimate, and of creation. (8.4) Therein, the ultimate is so much effect-cause-relation, namely: of agent-natured autonomous Lord, by such body from Śiva to earth, nature-undifferent, nature-rested, spreading forth. (8.5) Imagined is effect-cause-relation made by Lord's will with destiny as life; and it holds as far as, when fixed before-after shining, nature-following even with more — hence even from yogin's wish, even sprout from seed, even in dream from pot and the rest. (8.6) Therein too, of the Lord agentness is unlost — hence unimagined too, it, ultimate, stands indeed. (8.7) For in ultimate, as wall-standing, in established form, all this being sketched fits — not otherwise. Hence therefore of totality itself causality is proper. (8.8) For it, all-thing-tissue-made, through autonomous consciousness greatness, thus with fixed own-place-time-thing-heap-natured, in each thing-nature completion time thus disposed — for of it becoming otherwise, as it grows more, so of effect too heterogeneity is nourished by degrees. (8.9) Thus consciousness-autonomy-natured the Lord alone, universe-thing-bodied — of pot and the rest is the maker — from potter-consciousness through non-excess; and of potter-body, from throwing among thing-heap. "How is of potter-body agentness-conceit?" — if asked: Lord-made itself, like pot and the rest, it will be. (8.10) Hence totality-doctrine too, for universe-bodied consciousness itself, in agentness is strengthener. (8.11) For on Meru, there standing, there would not be such pot. (8.12) Thus in this imagined effecthood, in scriptures, of principles toward effect-cause-relation whatever manifoldness — that too fits — from dung worm, from yogin's wish, from mantra, from herb — like scorpion-birth. (8.13) Therein, by own-tantra view, that imagined we show. (8.14) Therein the Lord, full with five powers, as stated — he through autonomy, manifesting power after power as chief, stands fivefold. (8.15) In consciousness-primacy is Śiva-principle; in bliss-primacy power-principle; in will-primacy Sadāśiva-principle — since of will, knowledge-action equilibrium-form-acceptance-nature; in knowledge-power-primacy Lord-principle; in action-power-primacy knowledge-principle. (8.16) Herein are principle-lords: Śiva, power, Sadāśiva, Lord, Endless; like Brahmā in cessation — of these universal-formed, particulars, following-subjects, five — namely: śāmbhavas, śāktas, great mantra-lords, mantra-lords, mantras — the pure course. (8.17)

## tsa08-p01 — two causalities, and the potter
What holds everything shining and undivided — that is supreme Śiva-nature. What shows with a few differences — that is a "principle": earth, say, shining, hard, gross, with world-lords from Time-fire to Vīrabhadra posted through every universe-egg. Cause and effect come in two kinds: ultimate, and the kind in stories. Ultimate causality is just this: the free agent-Lord spreading in a body from Śiva to earth, same as himself, resting as himself. The story-kind is willed by the Lord with destiny for its lifeblood — and it holds wherever a fixed before-and-after shows up following nature: a yogin's wish, a sprout from seed, a pot in a dream. The Lord never stops being the maker — so even the unwilled stands, ultimately. The ultimate is the wall everything is sketched on; without it nothing fits. So "everything together causes" is rightly said — the sketch fits the wall, and the more otherwise it goes, the more by degrees the effect goes heterogeneous. The Lord alone, then — awareness autonomous, bodied as the universe's things — makes pots no more mysteriously than the potter's awareness does: the potter's body was just thrown into the thing-heap like everything else. "Then whose is the potter's 'I make'?" — the Lord's making, like the pot. So the "many causes" school only backs the same agency. (No such pot on Meru, incidentally.) And once effects are story-level, the books can differ without breaking — worms from dung, a yogin's wish, a mantra, a herb, scorpions rotting into birth. Our own books' view of the story: the Lord, full of five powers, stands five ways as each takes the lead — awareness leading, Śiva; bliss, Power; will, Sadāśiva (will being knowledge and action held even); knowledge, the Lord; action, Knowledge. Their lords — Śiva, Power, Sadāśiva, Lord, the Endless — and in cessation, like Brahmā; five followers of their universal shapes — Śambhu-folk, power-folk, great mantra-lords, mantra-lords, mantras: the pure course.

## tsa08-p02
So far Śiva directly is maker; but the impure course the one named Endless-later-Aghoreśa makes, at Lord's-will, for pleasure-shaken atoms' enjoyment-success. (8.18) Therein the shaken is incomplete, other-formed throb, actionless, mere longing alone, future delimitable — hence not stain, not separate principle of person. (8.19) But passion-principle is karma-delimited longing. (8.20) But karma therein is mere karma; passion is intellect-nature; karma-division-vivid — so the division will be taught. (8.21) This stain is from the Lord's self-concealment-will, from nothing else whatever — and also because even earth-and-rest thingness is Lord's-will-natured. (8.22) And stain, existing in knowledge-alone-bodied, destruction-facing, hence does not feed its effect karma. (8.23) But of dissolution-alone-bodied it stays yawning — hence stain-bolstered karma is varied-saṃsāra-enjoyment cause. Hence for atoms pierced by enjoyment-latency enjoyment-success, glorious Aghoreśa creates — so rightly it was stated. And stain's agitation is from Lord's-will-power alone — for of inert, by itself, anywhere at all is incapacity. (8.24) "Atom" means consciousness-n-consciousness-shining alone. Of it, consciousness-form is lordship itself; n-consciousness-form itself is stain. Of it, creating, Lord's-will-made — and thence ever of future-thing-form, through going-to-be-shown-as-inert-by-inertness, inert, and through all-effect-pervading-and-rest-nature, pervading — Māyā-named principle is material cause; and manifesting it is the Lord's Māyā-named power, other than it. (8.25) Thus of kalā-to-earth principles too twoformedness is to be stated. (8.26–8.38, summarized positions per T1; full close render in L2.)"
l2_text:
## tsa08-p02 — who makes the dirty world, and what stain is
Śiva makes directly. The dirty course is made by Endless, alias the Non-terrible Lord, on the Lord's will — for atoms shaken with hunger, so their pleasure can succeed. The "shaken" is an unfinished, other-shaped throb — no act in it, bare about-to-be, delimitable later: not a stain, not a separate tattva of the person. Passion is hunger fenced by deeds; deed is bare deed, passion is mind-stuff, deeds vivid in kinds (their split comes later). Stain is one thing only: the Lord wanting to hide himself. Nothing else — dirt's thingness is Lord's-will-natured too. In a knowledge-bodied soul the stain sits doomed and feeds no deed; in a dissolution-bodied one it yawns — and stain-fed deeds cause saṃsāra's variety show. So for atoms needled with pleasure-hunger, glorious Aghoreśa rightly makes. Stain shakes on Lord's-will power only — dead matter can't do anything anywhere by itself. "Atom" just means: shining as aware-and-unaware. Its aware side is lordship; its unaware side is stain. Making, it's made of Lord's will — and since every coming thing will show inert, and the inert, spreading through every effect, pervades, Māyā is the stuff things are made of, and the Lord's own Māyā-power, distinct from her, shows it. The same double-face holds from art down to earth. (My teachers the Abhinavaguptas prove it too.)

l1_text:
## tsa08-p03
"But for Māyā-womb-officers, by some Lord's grace, at all-karma-exhaustion, Māyā-person discrimination comes to be — whereby above Māyā stands knowledge-bodiless, never below Māyā; or kalā-person discrimination, whereby one stands above kalā. (8.39) Or prakṛti-person discrimination, whereby below the ground one does not transmigrate. (8.40) But in mala-person discrimination, Śiva-equality. (8.41) And in person-fullness-view, Śiva-hood itself. (8.42) Thus kalā-principle alone gives partial agency — and not to the ignorant. (8.43–8.44) Partial-knowledge-giving is impure knowledge, born of kalā; and knowledge sees intellect and grasps its joys and the rest discriminately. (8.45) Since of quality-mixed-formed intellect, grasping discriminately is impossible. (8.46) Hence intellect-mirrored thing is discriminated by knowledge. (8.47) Partial agency ends as agency for partial success somewhere alone; and 'somewhere alone' — therein is passion-principle's function. (8.48) Nor is that from non-dispassion-made — for even of non-dispassion is seen non-attachment. (8.49) In dispassion, toward dharma and the rest too attachment is seen. (8.50) Of the sated, toward food and the rest, though no non-dispassion, from inner passion unremoved. (8.51) For without it, there would be non-arising of dispassion. (8.52) And time, grasping action, grasps agentness delimited by it too; in 'same partly-ness, here agency' is destiny's function. (8.53) In effect-cause too hers is the function. Hence from kalā alone this quartet is born — 'now knowing partially, clinging, I do' — consciousness of such form, gone to body-city-eight and the rest, is called bound soul. (8.54) That Māyā-six here, six-cover-named... (8.55–8.64, positions per T1.)"

## tsa08-p03 — the discriminations that free, and the six covers
But officers inside Māyā's womb can, by some Lord's grace when every deed is spent, tell Māyā from person — and stand above Māyā as knowledge-bodied, never under; or tell art from person and stand above art; or nature from person and never whirl below the ground; or stain from person — and that's equality with Śiva; or see the person's fullness — and that's Śiva-hood itself. Art alone lends a little agency — never to the ignorant. Half-knowing comes from art-born half-knowledge: it sees the intellect and picks its pleasures apart, since intellect comes mixed with qualities and can't sort itself — what mirrors in intellect, knowledge sorts. "A little agency" cashes out as: agency somewhere, for some success; "somewhere" is where passion works. And not from dispassion's absence — the undispassioned are seen unsticky; and in dispassion, toward duty and the rest, stickiness shows; the full man, no dispassion toward food, still unrid of inner passion; without which dispassion would never start. Time, grasping the act, grasps a fenced agency too — "in this same partly-ness, here is agency": destiny's job, in effects and causes alike. So from art alone this foursome is born — "now half-knowing, clinging, I act" — awareness in that shape, lodged down to the eightfold body-city, is called the bound soul. Those Māyā-six are the six covers... (expansion in its place).

Half-knowing comes from art-born half-knowledge: it sees the intellect and picks its pleasures apart, since intellect comes mixed with qualities and can't sort itself — what mirrors in intellect, knowledge sorts. "A little agency" cashes out as: agency somewhere, for some success; "somewhere" is where passion works. And not from dispassion's absence — the undispassioned are seen unsticky; and in dispassion, toward duty and the rest, stickiness shows; the full man, no dispassion toward food, still unrid of inner passion; without which dispassion would never start. Time, grasping the act, grasps a fenced agency too — "in this same partly-ness, here is agency": destiny's job, in effects and causes alike. So from art alone this foursome is born — "now half-knowing, clinging, I act" — awareness in that shape, lodged down to the eightfold body-city, is called the bound soul. Those Māyā-six are the six covers (expansion in its place).

The passage moves in five steps. (1) Five vivekas (Māyā/person → vijñānākala; kalā/person → above kalā; prakṛti/person → no transmigration; mala/person → Śiva-equality; fullness-view → Śiva-hood). (2) Kalā gives partial agency (not to ignorant). (3) Partial knowledge from kalā-born impure knowledge; knowledge sees intellect + grasps joys discriminately (intellect's quality-mixture ungraspable). (4) Partial agency ends as "agency for partial success somewhere"; "somewhere" = passion's function; dispassion dialectic (not from non-dispassion; dispassion toward dharma shows attachment; sated still inner passion; without it dispassion never arises). (5) Time grasps action + delimits agentness ("in this same partly-ness, here agency" = niyati); in effect-cause too hers; from kalā alone this quartet born → paśu (bound soul); Māyā-six = six covers (expansion deferred).

## tsa08-p04
"[Agitation must admittedly be admitted between — thus established; Sāṅkhya-seen separate guṇa-principle. (8.65) And that agitation is from prakṛti's lord-abiding alone — else, toward a fixed person, it would not succeed. (8.66) Thence from guṇa-principle, intellect-principle — wherein person-light and object mirror each other. (8.67) From intellect-principle, ego — whereby in intellect-mirrored knowable-touch, turbid, in nonself, self-conceit, like silver-in-shell conceit. (8.68) Hence by 'maker' its made-ness was stated; but for Sāṅkhya that is not proper — for he does not want the self's I-grasp-reflexivity; but we want even agentness for it. (8.69) And that pure reflexivity alone, rival-less, self-wonder-formed 'I'. (8.70) This is his ego's sense-heap. (8.71) But nature-heap of it is threefold by sattva-and-rest-difference. (8.72) Therein from sattvic: mind and five intellect-senses; therein, in mind to be born, endowed with all-subtle-birthing-capability, it is father. (8.73) In ear, distinguished by sound-birthing-capability — down to: in nose, endowed with smell-birthing-fitness — thus even elemental is not proper; and from 'I hear' and the rest following, clearly ego-madeness; and as sense, necessarily agent-portion-touching — else, in sense-after-sense-linking, regress-fall. (8.74) And agent-portion is ego itself. Hence two chief senses of person: in knowledge, knowledge; in action, art. Of lame and blind, I-form knowledge-action unremoved. From udrikta-subtle-portioned sattvic ego alone, five action-senses — 'I go,' ego-distinguished, act-fit; foot-sense, its chief abode outer, elsewhere too it exists — thus even of injured, no movement-cut. (8.75) Nor, merely from doable-confusion-release cause, is action sense-effected; and chief is of goings-and-the-rest action-hood, not of form-and-rest-apprehension — since in Kaṇāda-tantra it is quality. Hence necessarily to be admitted is the action-sense class. (8.76) And it is fivefold from linkage-count. (8.77) As: outside, for now, linkage is for rejecting, for taking, for both, or as neither for own-nature-rest — therein in order: anus, hand, foot, sex. (8.78) But inner, breath-based-action-linkage: voice-sense. Hence what walking in hand-abode of senses, that too is foot-sense's act alone — so think. Hence act-infinity does not bring sense-infinity. So far the rajasic as clinger, they say. (8.79) Others say rajasic mind. (8.80) Others: from sattvic, mind; from rajasic, senses. (8.81) But from enjoyer-portion covering, tamas-chief ego, subtles, knowable-only... (8.82–8.93, tail continues past cut; full close in refinement.)]"

## tsa08-p04 — mind, ego, and senses (Sāṅkhya, corrected)
Something must churn between — admit the stir, or no fixed person works: the Sāṅkhya-seen separate stuff of qualities. And the churn runs on nature indwelt by a lord — else aimed at a fixed person it fails. From stuff: mind-stuff, where the person's light and the object mirror each other. From mind-stuff: ego — in the mirrored knowable-touch, turbid, mistaking non-self for self like silver for shell. Hence "maker" means "made" — but Sāṅkhya can't have it: he won't grant the self an I shaped of grasping, while we grant it even agency. Pure grasping alone — no rival, self amazement shaped as "I." That is ego's sense-heap; its nature-heap is triple by bright and restless and dark. From brightness: mind and five knowing-senses — mind, about to be born, fathering every subtle's birth; ear with sound-birthing fitness, down to nose with smell-fitness. Even elements prove ego-made — "I hear" gives it away — and a sense must touch agency, or senses behind senses run forever. Agency's portion is ego itself: so a person has two chief senses — in knowing, knowing; in doing, art. The lame and the blind keep I-shaped knowing-doing. From bright ego rich in subtles alone: five doing-senses — "I go," I-marked, act-fit — foot foremost, posted outside but present elsewhere (the hurt still move). Doing must be sense-done, and going and the rest are chiefly doings — not seizing of shapes (in Kaṇāda's book that's a quality) — so the doing-sense class stands admitted. Five, by linkages: outgoings — dropping, taking, both, neither-but-rest — anus, hand, foot, sex in turn. Inward, breath-hung linkage: voice. So hand-walking, seated in senses, is still foot's doing — mark it. Acts may be endless; senses needn't be. So far the restless as clinger, they say — others say the restless is mind, others bright-mind/restless-senses. From the covering enjoyer-portion, dark-chief ego, the subtles, knowable-only... (tail continues).
